newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian SAMECO aims to up aluminium product output.
newsitem.headline: Russian SAMECO aims to up aluminium product output.

text.p: The Samara Metallurgical Company (SAMECO), Russia's largest aluminium processing plant, aims to boost products output sharply in the next five years, partners in a marketing venture with SAMECO said on Tuesday.

Forecasts given in a news release by Reynolds International Inc of the United States and Sayansky Alyuminievy Zavod, Russia's third largest aluminium smelter, pointed to sharp increases at SAMECO starting in 1998.
"In addition to the production of aluminium can parts, SAMECO plans to increase production of other kinds of products to 55,000 tonnes in 1998 from 13,000 tonnes in 1997," the release said.
Product output would rise to 110,000 tonnes in 1999, 160,000 tonnes in 2000 and 215,000 tonnes in 2001, the release said.
The forecasts referred to finished or semi-finished products. SAMECO said in January it planned to boost production of rolled aluminium to 134,700 tonnes this year from 76,900 tonnes in 1996.
SAMECO also plans to start producing parts for aluminium cans, and expects to hit planned capacity of 60,000 tonnes by 1999. This would be in addition to the expected increase in products output.
The total will consist of 42,000 tonnes of can lids, 12,000 tonnes of can bodies and 6,000 tonnes of can rings.
The can parts will then be transported to an assembly plant, DOZAKL, which is scheduled to begin production of aluminium cans in April next year.

The initial output target at the plant is 1.5 billion cans annually. Reynolds and Sayansk pegged the total Russian aluminium can market at two to three billion a year, rising to over three billion by 2000.

Reynolds and the Sayansk smelter are already involved in a joint venture to produce aluminium foil in Russia. The Sayanal company is 70 percent owned by Sayansk, 15 percent by Reynolds and 15 percent by Fata of Italy.

Sayanal is currently exporting between 700 and 1,000 tonnes of aluminium products abroad and selling 300 to 500 tonnes to Russian customers, said Oleg Deripaska, general director of the Sayansk smelter.
He said he expected to see Russian demand for aluminium pick up, but slowly.

"I think this year we will see a small drop in Russian aluminium consumption, but that next year will be a year of growth," he said. "Demand in Russia will be around 180,000 tonnes during the first six months of the year."
Russia is the world's biggest aluminium exporter, delivering 2.44 million tonnes abroad in 1996.
